descriptionChirho: Qal stative: to be full, to be filled with something, describing a state of fullness (Arabic: امتلأ/مَلِيء, Korean: 가득하다/차다, Swahili: -jaa).
Niphal: to be filled, become full, receive filling as a passive or middle event (Arabic: امتلأ/يمتلئ Form VIII, Korean: 차다/채워지다, Swahili: -jazwa/-jaa).
Piel causative: to fill something or someone, to make full, actively causing fullness (Arabic: مَلَأَ/يَمْلَأُ, Korean: 채우다, Swahili: -jaza).

To fulfill a promise, complete a period, or bring to completion; a semantic extension from physical filling to abstract completion (Arabic: أَتَمَّ/اكتمال/تَمَّ, Korean: 성취하다/이루다, Swahili: -timiza/-kamilika).
Piel idiom 'mille acharei': to follow fully, to be wholly devoted to, used of loyal allegiance to God (Arabic: اتَّبَعَ, Korean: 충실히 따르다, Swahili: -fuata).
Piel/Pual specialized sense: to set or inlay precious stones into a mounting (Arabic: رَصَّعَ/ترصيع, Korean: 박히다, Swahili: -jazwa with gems context).
Piel extended sense: to satisfy hunger, thirst, or desire, filling as satiation (Arabic: يُشْبِعُ, Korean: 채우다 appetite, Swahili: -tosheleza).
Hitpael reflexive: to fill oneself, gather or mass together, reflexive filling (Arabic: يَتَجَمَّعُونَ, Korean: 채우다 reflexive, Swahili: -jikusanya).
Piel imperative used adverbially meaning 'fully, at full volume', intensifying rather than denoting physical filling (Arabic: اجمعوا, Korean: 가득 채우라, Swahili: kwa sauti kubwa).
Qal used transitively: to fill something, where Qal carries active transitive force rather than stative meaning (Arabic: مَلَأَ/مَلَأُوا, Korean: 채우다, Swahili: -jaza).
Qal infinitive used nominally: fullness, the state or measure of being full, in construct chains (Arabic: مِلْء, Korean: 풍족함/충만함, Swahili: wingi).
